### 1.  The condition about \(D\)

\(D\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle PQA\).  
Hence

\[
DP = DQ = DA .
\]

Since \(DA =1\), both \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on the circle  

\[
(x)^2+(y-1)^2=1\qquad\text{(center }D,\; \text{radius }1).
\tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  The condition about \(Q\)

\(Q\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle BPC\); therefore it is equidistant
from \(B\) and \(C\).  
The perpendicular bisector of \(BC\) is the horizontal line  

\[
y=\frac12 .
\tag{2}
\]

Thus \(Q\) must satisfy (2).  Intersecting (1) with (2),

\[
x^{2}+\Bigl(\frac12-1\Bigr)^2=1 \Longrightarrow x^{2}+ \frac14 =1
\Longrightarrow x^{2}= \frac34 .
\]

Hence

\[
Q=\Bigl(\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\ \frac12\Bigr).
\tag{3}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Computing \(|PQ|\)

Because \(Q\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle BPC\),

\[
QP = QB = QC .
\]

Consequently \(|PQ|\) equals the distance from \(Q\) to either \(B\) or \(C\).

*For \(Q =\bigl(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\frac12\bigr)\):*

\[
\begin{aligned}
QB^{2}&=\Bigl(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+ \Bigl(\frac12-0\Bigr)^{2}
      =\Bigl(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+ \frac14   \\[2mm]
      &=\Bigl(\frac{7}{4}-\sqrt3\Bigr)+\frac14
      =2-\sqrt3 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus  

\[
|PQ| = \sqrt{2-\sqrt3}.
\]

*For \(Q =\bigl(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\frac12\bigr)\):*

\[
\begin{aligned}
QB^{2}&=\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+ \frac14
      =\Bigl(\frac{7}{4}+\sqrt3\Bigr)+\frac14
      =2+\sqrt3 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence  

\[
|PQ| = \sqrt{2+\sqrt3}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Existence of the corresponding points \(P\)

For each of the two choices of \(Q\) the circles

\[
\begin{cases}
(x)^2+(y-1)^2 =1 &\text{(center }D)\\[2mm]
\bigl(x-x_Q\bigr)^2+\bigl(y-y_Q\bigr)^2 =|PQ|^2 &\text{(center }Q)
\end{cases}
\]

intersect in two points.  
One intersection is the degenerate case \(P=C\); the other gives a
non‑degenerate point \(P\) (e.g. \(P=(\tfrac12,\,1-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})\) for the first
\(Q\) and \(P=(\tfrac12,\,1+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})\) for the second).  
Thus both lengths are indeed attainable.
